research_rationale: EO 10513 designates the Assistant Secretaries of Labor and the Solicitor of Labor to act as Secretary of Labor when both the Secretary and the Under Secretary are unavailable, and supersedes EO 9968. It is one continuing standing designation (a single clause). Section 4 of EO 13245 (66 FR 66268, signed 2001-12-18) states "Executive Order 10513 of January 19, 1954, is hereby revoked." and EO 13245 has no later effective-date clause, so the revocation took effect on signing. The held texts that cite EO 10513 (EO 13245, the 1989 OFR codification note and the Federal Register page artifacts) show no earlier revocation, expiry or conditional end, and the status is a source-backed 'no' in the separate status decision.
savings_reason: The order created no accrued right, appointment or pending act: it only named who may act as Secretary of Labor on a vacancy or absence. EO 13245 replaced the designation with its own order of succession, and the bounded machine searches of current law (U.S. Code, eCFR) found no continuing independent rule citing EO 10513.
earlier_end_check: Searched held texts for the number 10513: only EO 13245 (revokes), the 1989 OFR note and FR page artifacts; no earlier revocation, supersession, expiry or lapse of the section 179 R.S. authority was found, and the supersession of EO 9968 is this order's own act, not an end.
scope_check: One continuing designation clause covering the Assistant Secretaries and the Solicitor; EO 13245 section 4 revokes the whole order, not a part.
independent_command_check: The sentence superseding EO 9968 was performed on issue and is part of the same paragraph; no independent surviving command exists.
savings_check: No savings or transfer provision in EO 10513 or EO 13245 section 4; nothing accrued under the designation.
